name: pwm_fpga_demo
description: FPGA-friendly LED breathing demo for board prototyping. The design uses a single clock input to generate a visible PWM fade pattern on one LED by combining a slow rate divider/counter, an 8-bit PWM counter, an 8-bit duty-cycle register, and a direction bit that ramps brightness up and down continuously. The contract is intended for synthesizable Lattice FPGA open-source flows such as Yosys and nextpnr, with starter board pin constraints to be generated separately after board selection and reviewed before hardware programming.

fixed_assumptions: Single-clock synchronous design using clk only.

No asynchronous reset is required; registers power up to a defined synthesis-safe state only if supported by the implementation flow, otherwise rely on local initialization and/or board startup behavior appropriate for the selected FPGA family.
LED output is active-high unless a board-specific constraint review later requires inversion at the board level.
The breathing effect must be visually apparent to a human observer and should update slowly relative to the PWM carrier frequency.

functionality: Top-level PWM LED demo. On every clk edge, the logic advances an 8-bit PWM carrier counter continuously and compares it against an 8-bit duty-cycle register to drive led. A slower internal counter periodically steps the duty-cycle register upward or downward. A direction bit controls whether the duty cycle increments or decrements at each slow step, causing the LED brightness to breathe smoothly between low and high intensity. The implementation must be fully synthesizable, use only standard RTL constructs, and avoid ASIC-only, testbench-only, or vendor-specific primitives in the top module.
responsibilities: Generate a stable PWM carrier using an 8-bit counter.
Compare the carrier against an 8-bit duty-cycle register to produce the LED PWM output.
Create a slower enable/update event from a counter derived from clk.
Ramp the duty cycle up and down using a direction bit to create a breathing effect.
Keep the implementation simple, portable, and acceptable to lint, synthesis, and place-and-route flows.
must_not_drive: Any additional top-level I/O, clocks, resets, memories, or vendor-specific resources.
Any ASIC-only constructs, delays, real-number types, DPI, or testbench-only signals.
reset_behavior: No explicit reset port is defined for this demo. Internal sequential state should start from a benign, synthesis-friendly condition consistent with FPGA initialization behavior or local initialization in RTL, with duty cycle and direction arranged so the LED begins in a low-brightness or mid-brightness state and then enters the breathing sequence after configuration.
behavior_rules: Use a single synchronous clock domain driven only by clk.
Implement an 8-bit duty-cycle register that is compared against the PWM counter to determine led state.
Implement a slow counter or divider that creates a visible brightness update rate much lower than the PWM carrier frequency.
Use a direction bit to alternate the duty-cycle ramp between incrementing and decrementing.
Clamp or reverse the duty-cycle ramp at the minimum and maximum bounds so the sequence repeats continuously.
Do not instantiate memories, macros, or vendor primitives in the top module.
Do not use non-synthesizable timing constructs, behavioral delays, or real-number math.
Keep the design compatible with Lattice open-source flows and straightforward timing review.
